purpose: Concept illustrations for the RoboFalcon project showcase. Illustrations are not records of completed experiments or built hardware.

assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: wide 16:9 illustration for the future research section of an executive bio-inspired flight website. Primary request: a refined engineering concept visualization of a flapping-wing robotic bird progressing from precision components to an assembled prototype. Scene: a clean warm ivory studio workbench. Subject: one elegant small bird-like mechanical airframe with two articulated wings, restrained carbon-fibre spars, machined aluminium joints, pale translucent membrane, with a few matching components arranged neatly beside it. Clearly an illustrative design concept, not a photograph of a built project and not a verified mechanical topology. Style: premium industrial design visualization with realistic materials and softly simplified engineering detail, disciplined, credible, no science-fiction. Composition: three-quarter overhead view, entire prototype and both wings in frame, balanced airy wide composition; no labels or typography. Color palette: warm ivory, graphite, desaturated sage green, subtle silver; matches an ink-green and warm-white website. Soft studio shadows, museum-quality presentation. Avoid text, logos, watermarks, invented dimension lines, fake graphs, glowing neon, people, propellers or jet engines.

Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: wide 16:9 editorial concept illustration for a bio-inspired flight project's future research website. Primary request: show three distinct falcon flight phases in one refined, coherent, evenly spaced horizontal triptych: left a falcon rising after take-off with powerful downstroke and feet pulling upward; centre a falcon in level forward flapping flight with streamlined body; right a falcon braking for landing with wings raised, tail fanned and feet reaching forward. Three separate birds, one per phase; all fly toward the right. Entire birds and all wings visible with clear space between them; anatomically plausible falcons with exactly two wings and two legs, realistic feather structure. This is an explanatory illustration, not actual captured experimental data. Style: beautifully rendered natural-history editorial illustration with soft dimensional realism and a restrained modern presentation, not cartoon, not photomontage. Background warm light ivory, very subtle ground shadows, no landscape clutter. Colors natural falcon browns and slate greys, restrained sage undertones. No text, labels, borders, arrows, logos, watermarks, duplicate wings, plotted curves, or numeric annotations.

Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: wide 16:9 concept illustration for an executive research website, wind-tunnel measurement preparation. Primary request: a credible conceptual wind-tunnel test setup using a robotic flapping-wing bird as a surrogate for later real-bird wing-trajectory measurements. Subject: one small bird-shaped articulated wing robot positioned in the open visible test section of a compact low-speed research wind tunnel, with a discreet lower support mount, two machine-vision cameras outside the transparent sidewalls at complementary front-oblique and side viewing angles, and soft LED illumination. Bird has two articulated membrane wings, graphite spars, silver joints, recognisably mechanical rather than a real animal. Show tunnel opening and flow-straightener at far end, clear uncluttered view of test volume, tasteful translucent suggestion of airflow, not dense arbitrary lines. Style: premium engineering cutaway/concept rendering, precise calm editorial 3D, not documentary evidence of actual equipment. Palette: deep desaturated ink-green and graphite background with warm ivory light, muted sage accents and aluminium. Composition wide three-quarter view, entire setup visible and cameras not obscuring specimen, logical camera lines of sight. No text, no labels, no dimensions, no logos, no fake measured data, no people, no lasers, no sci-fi holograms.
